correctness.rationale: Multiplication of the source PMF, gamma density, and conditional exponential-minimum density forces the factors 1/[-log(1-eta)] and 1/Gamma(lambda). They depend on optimized parameters and cannot be discarded as proportionality constants. The literal Eq. (4.5) then has positive m lambda log lambda growth and is unbounded as the frailty shape increases. With the missing log-Gamma term restored, Stirling cancellation and the inequality 1+log z-z<=0 make the corrected auxiliary function tend to minus infinity at the right endpoint; the gamma pole gives the same at the left endpoint. The packaged checker verifies the corrected score derivatives and the box-boundary behavior of the printed objective.

value.rationale: The paper presents a three-parameter EM procedure and attributes joint-parameter instability primarily to weak identifiability. As printed, however, the frailty-shape M-step has no finite optimum at all, so a box-constrained routine is necessarily cap-dependent rather than an EM maximization of the stated model. Restoring the two normalizers gives the exact eta and lambda scores and separates a structural algebraic defect from genuine weak-identifiability behavior. This is consequential for anyone reproducing or extending the method, while the claim is carefully limited so it does not impugn the fixed-lambda simulation or direct-likelihood real-data fit.
